I am 53 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou County for over thirty years. My father taught me how to read the soil and the weather, and I finished middle school, which was enough to understand the basics of what the seed dealers and extension workers tell me. I hold about 10 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain.

For me, there is only one sensible system: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I have tried other crops in the past, but the wheat-maize rotation is what the land, the climate, and the market reward here. The wheat goes in after National Day in October, sleeps through the cold months, and comes off the field in early June. The very same day, or the next, I put the maize in. Every year it is a race against autumn frost, so I do not waste a single day.

I till before wheat with the rotary tiller to break up the corn stubble and level the seedbed. For the maize, there is no time for ploughing — I seed directly into the wheat stubble. I buy improved wheat seed from the county seed station; for maize I always use hybrid seed, usually a package per mu, because the hybrids yield better and the grain buyers pay well for uniform kernels. 

Fertiliser is the backbone of the crop. For wheat I spread compound fertiliser at sowing and then top-dress with urea at green-up and jointing. Maize gets a basal compound application when I sow it, and sometimes I side-dress more nitrogen if the plants look pale by the knee-high stage. I irrigate from my well. Wheat needs water at green-up, jointing, heading, and grain-filling — four times in a normal year. Maize is tougher; twice is usually enough, once at the seedling stage and once at the big flare stage. 

Pests and weeds are handled the same way my neighbours do them: a herbicide spray early, then insecticide when I see aphids or corn borers, and a fungicide on the wheat if the weather turns damp around heading. I do not take chances with weeds — one spray is cheaper than hand-weeding 10 mu.

I expect about 1,100 jin of wheat per mu and about 1,150 jin of maize per mu if the rains come on time and the well does not run dry.
